records.label: Older sib
quotes: Two sibs with a syndrome including cleft lip and palate, sparse scalp hair, malformed protruding ears, and partial syndactyly of the fingers and toes are reported.
The older child also has mental retardation and pili torti.

records.label: Younger sib
quotes: Two sibs with a syndrome including cleft lip and palate, sparse scalp hair, malformed protruding ears, and partial syndactyly of the fingers and toes are reported.

records.label: Two Turkish brothers
quotes: Two Turkish sibs, products of a second cousin marriage, with tetramelic syndactyly, ectodermal dysplasia, cleft lip and palate, renal anomalies, and mental retardation are reported.

records.label: 3 Brazilian brothers
quotes: We report on 3 Brazilian brothers born to normal consanguineous parents (F = 1/16) and presenting ectodermal dysplasia, cleft lip/palate, mental retardation, syndactyly of fingers 2-3, accessory nipples, and ear anomalies.

records.label: 27 affected individuals from 7 related families, Margarita Island
records.segregation: All parents normal; females affected as severely as males
quotes: We describe 27 individuals of 7 families related to each other with high probability who showed manifestations of ectodermal dysplasia and other anomalies affecting females as severely as males with variable expressivity. All parents were normal.

These families were detected in a relatively isolated and inbred population with very small neighbouring communities from a Caribbean Sea island, Margarita Island, in Northeastern Venezuela (Nueva Esparta State).

records.label: Four Margarita Island ED4 families
quotes: Haplotype analysis of four complex Margarita Island ED4 families localized the ED4 gene to an approximately 1-2-Mb interval spanned by just two YACs.

records.label: Sporadic non-syndromic CL/P patients, northern Venezuela

phenotypes.text: non-syndromic cleft lip with or without cleft palate

quotes: Here we demonstrate highly significant association between heterozygosity for this mutation and sporadic, non-syndromic CL/P in northern Venezuela.

records.label: 7-year-old Japanese boy
quotes: A 7-year-old Japanese boy, the first child of a consanguineous marriage, showed hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia with sparse, brittle, fine, dry hair and hypodontia, the unique facial appearance with cleft lip/palate, cutaneous syndactyly of the fingers and mild mental retardation.
Scanning electron microscopic examination of the hair demonstrated pili torti and pili trianguli et canaliculi.
Mutation analysis of exon 2 of PVRL1 revealed a novel homozygous nonsense mutation, c.400C>T (p.Arg134*). His parents were heterozygous for the mutant alleles.

notes.statement: Yoshida et al. (2015) noted that all 4 PVRL1 mutations identified in cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome to date, including theirs, resulted in truncated proteins lacking the transmembrane and intracellular domains of nectin-1, which are necessary to initiate cell-cell adhesion.
quotes: All four PVRL1 mutations identified in cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome to date, including this study, resulted in truncated proteins that lack the transmembrane domain and intracellular domain of nectin-1, which is necessary to initiate the cell-cell adhesion process.

notes.statement: Yoshida et al. (2015) reported what they believed to be the first Asian individual with cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome.
quotes: We present the first report, to our knowledge, of an Asian individual with cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome with a novel PVRL1 mutation.

notes.statement: Sözen et al. (2001) found a highly significant association between heterozygosity for the PVRL1 nonsense mutation W185X, which in the homozygous state causes the autosomal recessive CL/P syndrome CLPED1 on Margarita Island, and sporadic, non-syndromic cleft lip with or without cleft palate in northern Venezuela.
quotes: Homozygosity for a nonsense mutation of PVRL1, W185X, results in an autosomal recessive CL/P syndrome on Margarita Island, CLPED1 (ref. 1).
Here we demonstrate highly significant association between heterozygosity for this mutation and sporadic, non-syndromic CL/P in northern Venezuela.

notes.statement: Suzuki et al. (2000) used positional cloning to identify PVRL1 as the gene responsible for autosomal recessive cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome (CLPED1). PVRL1 encodes nectin-1, an immunoglobulin-related transmembrane cell-cell adhesion molecule of the NAP cell adhesion system.
quotes: Here we describe positional cloning of the gene responsible for an autosomal recessive CL/P-ectodermal dysplasia (ED) syndrome (CLPED1; previously ED4; ref. 2), which we identify as PVRL1, encoding nectin-1, an immunoglobulin (Ig)-related transmembrane cell-cell adhesion molecule that is part of the NAP cell adhesion system.

notes.statement: Suzuki et al. (2000) noted that CLPED1 is common on Margarita Island in the Caribbean Sea. Because nectin-1 is the main cell surface receptor for alpha-herpesviruses (HveC), they suggested that this high frequency might be due to heterozygotes being resistant to infection by these viruses.
quotes: Nectin-1 is also the principal cell surface receptor for alpha-herpesviruses (HveC; ref. 7), and the high frequency of CLPED1 on Margarita Island in the Caribbean Sea might result from resistance of heterozygotes to infection by these viruses.

notes.statement: Suzuki et al. (2000) noted that CLPED1 was previously designated ED4.
quotes: (CLPED1; previously ED4; ref. 2)

notes.statement: Suzuki et al. (1998) described Margarita Island ectodermal dysplasia (ED4) as an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by unusual facies, dental anomalies, hypotrichosis, palmoplantar hyperkeratosis and onychodysplasia, syndactyly, and cleft lip/cleft palate.
quotes: Margarita Island ectodermal dysplasia (ED4) is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by unusual facies, dental anomalies, hypotrichosis, palmoplantar hyperkeratosis and onychodysplasia, syndactyly, and cleft lip/cleft palate.

notes.statement: Using an affected-only DNA-pooling strategy, Suzuki et al. (1998) carried out linkage disequilibrium mapping of the ED4 gene to 11q23. Haplotype analysis of 4 complex Margarita Island families localized the gene to an approximately 1- to 2-Mb interval spanned by just 2 YACs.
quotes: We have used an affected-only DNA-pooling strategy to carry out linkage disequilibrium mapping of the ED4 gene to 11q23.
Haplotype analysis of four complex Margarita Island ED4 families localized the ED4 gene to an approximately 1-2-Mb interval spanned by just two YACs.

notes.statement: Zlotogora (1994) described the association of syndactyly, ectodermal dysplasia, and cleft lip/palate.
quotes: Syndactyly, ectodermal dysplasia, and cleft lip/palate.

notes.statement: Zlotogora et al. (1987) concluded that the syndrome of cleft lip and palate, sparse scalp hair, malformed ears, and partial syndactyly that they described in 2 sibs was most probably inherited as an autosomal recessive disorder.
quotes: This syndrome is most probably inherited as an autosomal recessive disorder.

notes.statement: Zlotogora and Ogur (1988) reported on the association of syndactyly, ectodermal dysplasia, and cleft lip and palate.
quotes: Syndactyly, ectodermal dysplasia, and cleft lip and palate.

notes.statement: Rodini and Richieri-Costa (1990) reported 3 affected brothers born to normal consanguineous parents (F = 1/16). They discussed the pattern of inheritance as autosomal recessive.
quotes: Autosomal recessive ectodermal dysplasia, cleft lip/palate, mental retardation, and syndactyly: the Zlotogora-Ogur syndrome.
We report on 3 Brazilian brothers born to normal consanguineous parents (F = 1/16)

notes.statement: Bustos et al. (1991) concluded that the disorder was a newly recognized autosomal recessive dysplasia/malformation syndrome. Females were affected as severely as males, all parents were normal, and the families came from a relatively isolated, inbred population.
quotes: We believe that this condition constitutes a newly recognized autosomal recessive dysplasia/malformation syndrome of ectodermal dysplasia.
affecting females as severely as males with variable expressivity. All parents were normal.

notes.statement: Bustos et al. (1991) found that the clinical picture shared by all patients could not be classified within the known ectodermal dysplasias. They also stated that previously published cases did not resemble their patients.
quotes: The clinical picture common to all patients could not be classified within the heterogeneous group of known ectodermal dysplasias and the published cases do not resemble our patients.
